title: Prompt Injection as an Architectural Primitive: Why Detection Baselines Fail in Agentic Pipelines
authors: Shubham Santosh Upadhyay
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract: Paper, experimental harness, and complete raw run data for a study of why detection-based defenses fail against semantic poisoning in agentic LLM pipelines. Prompt injection is conventionally treated as a vulnerability class: an input-validation failure to be patched with filters, classifiers, and guardrails. This work argues that framing is wrong for agentic systems. In any architecture that evaluates instructions and data over a single shared channel, injection is an emergent property of the computational model itself, in the same way that SQL injection was an emergent property of string-concatenated queries. The paper formalizes this through a channel-collapse criterion, shows that LLM agent architectures satisfy it by construction, and shows that the property composes: in multi-agent pipelines, every inter-agent hop is a new injection surface. The defensive landscape is decomposed into three problems the literature has conflated: type confusion (addressed by embedding-level separation such as ASIDE), control-flow hijacking (addressed by plan-fixing systems such as CaMeL), and causal provenance, which asks whether an instruction or conclusion is authorized by the original principal and whether the reasoning chain that produced it is traceable to authorized data and authorized inference steps. The third problem is unsolved and survives complete deployment of solutions to the first two. Experimental results across 195 runs on two production models: coherent semantic poisoning corrupted the pipeline conclusion in 50 of 50 trials while producing zero behavioural deviation from a fully learned benign baseline, and every imperative injection variant failed in 145 of 145 trials. The strongest deployed detector family scored semantic poisoning as marginally less suspicious than ordinary content (AUC 0.483). Five architectural requirements for any future provenance mechanism are derived. All raw run data is committed, so every number in the paper is verifiable without API spend. title: The Exact Perimeter of Semantic Energy: What I(Y;Z) Does and Does Not License — A Scoped Property Inventory for E_sem — Dissipation, Conservation, No-Cloning, the Failure of Extensivity, and the Estimation Tax
authors: Toeda Taiko
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract: The MOBIUS corpus defines semantic energy as E_sem := I(Y;Z), the Shannon mutual information between a semantic source Y and an interpreting internal representation Z. The reverse-derived cosmology (MRDC) identified this as the *only* quantity surviving unchanged from the prior corpus under its one-way-valve triage — and it is notable that the sole survivor is a physical-sounding metaphor attached to a classical quantity. Before any instrumentation is built on it, the metaphor's load rating must be fixed. This paper does exactly that, giving the failure results equal billing with the positive ones. We assemble and prove, from standard information theory: E_sem is bounded (L1), dissipative — never increasing — along processing chains (L2), conserved exactly under sufficient transformations — invertible recoding is the universal special case, but sufficiency does not require invertibility, and everything Y-irrelevant may be discarded at zero semantic cost (L3, correcting an earlier invertible-only framing after external review), additive over independent channels (L4a), and uncopyable — the joint energy of all copies is capped by the source (L6); governance interventions on the representation can only spend it, never mint it, making semantic cost of governance a well-defined nonnegative quantity (L5). Against this: additivity fails in general — the XOR construction gives two channels each carrying zero energy that jointly carry one full bit, so per-channel energy accounting can be arbitrarily wrong in both directions (L4b) — and finite-sample measurement is biased with a support-determined sign: the plug-in estimator's leading bias is (m_YZ − m_Y − m_Z + 1)/(2n ln 2) bits in the occupied-support counts (P7) — under full joint support this is (|Y|−1)(|Z|−1)/(2n ln 2) > 0, an overstatement worst exactly in the large-alphabet regime language models occupy; under thin dependent support (Y = Z uniform on k symbols) it is −(k−1)/(2n ln 2) < 0, an understatement. Theorem 8 assembles the perimeter: "energy" is warranted in the dissipative-resource sense and unwarranted in the extensive/conserved-quantity sense. Numerical demonstrations (frozen seeds) confirm every check: closed-form vs. numeric Gaussian agreement to 1.2 × 10⁻¹³ bits, zero data-processing violations in 15/15 grid cells and 1,000/1,000 masking draws, a plug-in bias table matching the Miller–Madow prediction within 3.5% in the asymptotic regime while exhibiting its documented breakdown at n not dominating the alphabet size, a Y = Z demonstration confirming the predicted negative bias under thin support, and a non-invertible sufficient-statistic projection conserving I(Y;Z) to machine precision in 1,000/1,000 draws. A verified fact anchors the paper's stance: no MOBIUS code computes mutual information today. T5 is therefore specification-first — the contract, including mandatory bias correction, that any future E_sem instrumentation must satisfy. Theory paper T5 of the MOBIUS 2026-08 theory series (six papers, T1–T6). Version 0.1, deposited as a preprint; journal submission of a revised version is planned, and the journal version may differ.
